description: Internal 50-query recall set (§14: ≥80% top-3, CI-gated). Planted memories simulate a developer's store; queries mix exact keywords and light paraphrase. CI runs with the deterministic hash embedder + BM25 — the offline floor; the local model can only improve on it.

memories.content: User prefers pytest over unittest for all Python projects.
User prefers tabs for indentation in Go and Makefiles.
User prefers conventional commit messages with a scope, like feat(api): add rate limits.
User prefers dark editor themes; Solarized Dark in VS Code.
User prefers small pull requests under 400 lines for review.
User prefers TypeScript strict mode enabled on every new frontend package.
User runs golangci-lint before every push and expects zero warnings.
Alice Chen prefers async standups posted in the #eng-daily Slack channel.
The team decided to use gRPC instead of REST for the internal service mesh.
The team decided to keep the monorepo; splitting repos was rejected in the March review.
Auth uses JWT access tokens with a 15-minute expiry and rotating refresh tokens.
The staging database is Postgres 16 running on RDS.
The billing service deploys to Fly.io on Friday afternoons.
The retry budget for outbound webhooks is 3 attempts with exponential backoff.
The public API rate limit is 250 requests per minute per key.
The default branch is main; release branches are cut as release/YYYY-MM.
The Redis cache TTL for session data is 300 seconds.
Production runs in AWS us-east-1 with a warm standby in us-west-2.
The team uses Linear for issue tracking; ticket ids look like ENG-1234.
The frontend uses pnpm workspaces for package management.
Errors are reported to Sentry under the acme-platform organization.
Secrets are managed in HashiCorp Vault; nothing is stored in environment files.
Protobuf definitions live in the proto/ directory and generate Go and TypeScript clients.
User uploads land in the acme-uploads-prod S3 bucket with 30-day lifecycle rules.
On-call rotates weekly on Mondays through PagerDuty.
Local development uses docker compose with the make dev target.
Database migrations run through Atlas, never raw SQL in production.
Feature flags are served by LaunchDarkly; the SDK key lives in Vault.
The mobile app talks to the GraphQL gateway, not to services directly.
The team decided CI fails below 80 percent test coverage on changed packages.
Bob Tanaka owns the Kubernetes cluster configuration and Helm charts.
The design system package is @acme/prism; components are documented in Storybook.
Releases ship every other Wednesday on the release train.
Hotfixes require two approvals and a green smoke suite before deploy.
The data pipeline is pinned to Python 3.12 because of a pandas compatibility issue.
Nightly ETL jobs run in Airflow at 02:00 UTC.
Every service directory keeps a runbook.md with oncall procedures.
Infrastructure changes go through Terraform in the infra repo; console changes are forbidden.
Dashboards live in Grafana; the golden signals board is called Platform Overview.
The API availability SLO is 99.9 percent measured monthly.
Background jobs go through SQS with a dead letter queue after 5 receives.
Transactional email is sent through Postmark, not SES.
Payments are processed by Stripe; webhooks are verified with the signing secret from Vault.
The web app is localized with i18next; strings live in locales/ JSON files.
The support matrix is the last two versions of Chrome, Firefox, Safari, and Edge.
Services log JSON lines to stdout; Loki aggregates them.
Public API documentation is generated from the OpenAPI spec in api/openapi.yaml.
Staging login uses the shared demo tenant named wonderland.
The frontend performance budget is 200KB of JavaScript per route.
Quarterly access reviews happen in the first week of each quarter.
Internal Go modules are proxied through Athens at goproxy.internal.acme.dev.
Production SSH goes through the bastion host; direct node access is disabled.
Wednesdays are meeting-free focus days for the platform team.
Product specs live in Notion under the Roadmap wiki.
Sprint retros happen every second Thursday and produce three action items max.
